items.title: NCSC-2026-0506 [1.00] [H/H] Kwetsbaarheden verholpen in NGINX door F5 Networks
items.excerpt: F5 Networks heeft meerdere kwetsbaarheden verholpen in NGINX Plus en NGINX Open Source. De kwetsbaarheden betreffen verschillende onderdelen en configuraties van NGINX. De belangrijkste kwetsbaarheid met kenmerk CVE-2026-123007 stelt kwaadwillenden in staat om willekeurige code uit te voeren op het onderliggende systeem. Het NCSC verwacht dat er op korte termijn proof of concept code beschikbaar komt, waarna exploitatie op grote schaal verwacht wordt.

items.title: The challenge of defending against bulletproof dead drops on public blockchains
items.excerpt: The evolution of malware command-and-control (C2) infrastructure has shifted away from fragile, centralized servers and hardcoded domains toward resilient, decentralized blockchain networks that eliminate single points of failure.

items.title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
items.excerpt: Written by: Jayson Frost, Bryce Greathouse, Dhanesh Kizhakkinan, John Palmisano, Steve Rasch, Daniel Sislo, John Wolfram Introduction On Oct. 15, 2026, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) published a blog post detailing recent activity in which the suspected PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly tracked as UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-102764, a zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support, which was patched in BT26-05 . We also described some of the threat actor’s post-exploitation operations. In this blog we describe additional post-compromise activity involving the exploitation of a vulnerability in VMware vCenter and the deployment of additional malware families. On Nov. 19, 2026, VMware disclosed CVE-2026-123890, which impacts VMware vCenter Server deployments. vSphere consists of both ESXi (the hypervisor) and vCenter Server. The vCenter server is a centralized platform deployed as a Photon Linux virtual appliance and is used to configure, control, and monitor ESXi host environments.
